title: Can GenAI improve students’ mathematics learning outcomes effectively?—A meta-analysis of empirical research 2023-2025
extended_summary:
This paper addresses whether generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), including tools such as ChatGPT and other large language models, improves students’ mathematics learning outcomes. It was written as a systematic review and meta-analysis of empirical studies published from 2023 to 2025, motivated by mixed prior findings and the lack of a mathematics-specific synthesis.

The review aggregates experimental and quasi-experimental studies comparing GenAI-supported mathematics instruction with traditional teaching. Outcomes were organized into cognitive skills and non-cognitive skills, with cognitive outcomes further split into higher-order and lower-order thinking. The analysis also examined moderators such as educational level, intervention duration, learning content, GenAI integration level, and sample size.

The included evidence covered primary school, middle school, high school, and undergraduate students. The review found an overall positive effect of GenAI on mathematics learning outcomes, with stronger effects for cognitive than non-cognitive outcomes. The most favorable effects appeared for higher-order cognition, elementary students, and interventions classified as creative transformation under the PIC-RAT framework. Smaller studies showed larger effects, while intervention duration and learning content were not significant moderators.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis with a clearly specified search window, inclusion criteria, quality appraisal (MERSQI), bias checks, and moderator analyses. Those features make it high-quality evidence despite being a protocol-style report rather than a completed journal meta-analysis article.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effect on mathematics learning outcomes is moderate and positive (g = 0.539), exceeding the threshold for medium impact. The strongest gains appear in priority K-12 subgroups, especially elementary students and creative-transformation use cases.

interventions.use_case: Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and other large language models used in mathematics instruction for personalized tutoring, step-by-step problem solving, conceptual explanations, interactive dialogue, and feedback generation.

finding.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 22 empirical studies (46 effect sizes; N=5,132) found a moderate positive overall effect of GenAI on mathematics learning outcomes, with pooled Hedges' g = 0.539 (p < .005). The effect was stronger for cognitive outcomes (g = 0.596) than for non-cognitive outcomes (g = 0.320), and especially strong for higher-order cognitive skills (g = 0.740) compared with lower-order skills (g = 0.562).
finding.measure: Mathematics learning outcomes; cognitive skill outcomes (higher-order and lower-order) and overall achievement/learning measures

finding.finding_summary: Across the non-cognitive outcome set, GenAI showed a positive but smaller pooled effect (g = 0.320) on motivational and affective variables such as anxiety, self-efficacy, engagement, and attitudes. The review reports these effects as favorable overall, but clearly weaker than the cognitive gains.
finding.measure: Math anxiety, self-efficacy, motivation, engagement, attitudes

finding.finding_summary: For cognitive skills that map to durable skills, GenAI had a stronger effect on higher-order thinking outcomes such as analysis, evaluation, creation, and complex problem-solving (g = 0.740) than on lower-order thinking (g = 0.562). This indicates a comparatively larger benefit for deeper reasoning and metacognitive-type performance in mathematics learning.
